stem:
Rudo made a temporary mount of onion epidermis stained with iodine solution and observed it with the ×10 objective lens.

Calibration: with the ×10 objective, 50 eyepiece graticule divisions lined up exactly with 48 divisions of a stage micrometer. Each stage micrometer division is 0.01 mm.

She then measured the lengths of five cells in eyepiece divisions:

| Cell | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Length / eyepiece divisions | 22 | 25 | 19 | 24 | 20 |

The cells were elongated, roughly rectangular and arranged in rows with their ends touching. Each had a thin layer of cytoplasm against the wall, a large clear vacuole, and a stained nucleus usually near one side wall.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the length of one eyepiece division in µm.
parts.explanation: 48 × 10 µm = 480 µm; 480 ÷ 50 = 9.6 µm. Dividing 50 by 48 and multiplying by 10 gives 10.4.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 48 × 10 µm = 480 µm; 480 ÷ 50 = 9.6 µm. Dividing 50 by 48 and multiplying by 10 gives 10.4.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the mean length of the five cells in eyepiece divisions.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the mean actual length of the cells in µm, to three significant figures.
parts.explanation: 22 × 9.6 = 211.2, which is 211 µm to three significant figures. Assuming one division is 10 µm (no calibration) gives 220; leaving the micrometer in mm gives 0.211.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 22 × 9.6 = 211.2, which is 211 µm to three significant figures. Assuming one division is 10 µm (no calibration) gives 220; leaving the micrometer in mm gives 0.211.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Rudo made a high-power drawing of three adjacent cells. Describe what a drawing that meets the practical-paper conventions would show.

points.description: Clear, sharp, continuous lines (pencil); no shading or colouring
Cell walls drawn as double lines, with shared walls between adjacent cells; correct elongated shape and proportions of the three cells
Only observable contents: nucleus (with nucleolus if seen) near the wall, thin layer of cytoplasm, vacuole not shaded; no structures not seen (no chloroplasts)
Labels (cell wall, nucleus, cytoplasm, vacuole) with ruled label lines that touch the structure and do not cross; drawing large (fills most of the space)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A large pencil drawing of three touching, elongated cells in correct proportion, with each cell wall drawn as a double line and shared walls between cells. Lines are sharp and unbroken, with no shading. Each cell shows a nucleus against a side wall and a thin layer of cytoplasm, the vacuole left unshaded; no chloroplasts are drawn because none were seen. Labels for cell wall, cytoplasm, nucleus and vacuole are joined by ruled lines that touch the structures and do not cross.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Cell 4 (24 eyepiece divisions) was drawn 70 mm long. Calculate the magnification of the drawing, to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Rudo also observed cheek cells stained with methylene blue. State **three** observable differences between the onion epidermal cells and the cheek cells that she could record in a table.

points.description: Onion: cell wall present (thick outline); cheek: no cell wall, only a thin membrane
Onion: regular, elongated rectangular cells in rows; cheek: irregular, flattened, rounded cells, often separate or overlapping
Onion: large vacuole with thin peripheral cytoplasm and nucleus at the side; cheek: no large vacuole, nucleus central (or onion much larger than cheek cells)

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: 

| Feature | Onion epidermal cell | Cheek cell |
|---|---|---|
| Cell wall | Present | Absent |
| Shape | Regular, elongated, in rows | Irregular, rounded, separate |
| Vacuole and nucleus | Large vacuole; nucleus at the side | No large vacuole; nucleus central |

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Explain why Rudo measured five cells and calculated a mean rather than measuring one cell.

points.description: Cells vary in length (19 to 25 divisions)
A mean of several measurements is more representative / reliable, reducing the effect of one unusual cell

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The cells vary in length, from 19 to 25 divisions, so a single cell may not be typical; a mean of several cells gives a more representative and reliable estimate of cell length.

explanation: Calibrate first (9.6 µm per division at ×10), multiply the mean divisions by the calibration (211 µm), and use actual size for the drawing's magnification (×304). Drawings show only what is seen, with clear lines, double walls and ruled labels.
hints: One eyepiece division = (stage divisions × 10 µm) ÷ eyepiece divisions.
Convert the drawing length to µm before dividing.
